name: Runtime
oneLiner: Firecracker microVMs billed on measured CPU, with the strongest secret handling in this set.
whatItIs: Runtime Cloud is a hosted fleet of Firecracker microVMs that an agent, or the program driving it, creates, runs commands in, pauses, forks and deletes over an API.

It is sold as compute for AI-agent workloads rather than websites or long-lived servers. The commercial pitch is that CPU is billed on measured use with a very low idle floor, so a sandbox waiting on a language model costs almost nothing.

Twenty products sit behind one API, CLI, MCP server and SDK set: sandboxes, secrets, images, volumes, snapshots, previews, desktop, metrics, webhooks, OpenTelemetry, TCP ports, private networks and more.
whoFor: Teams building agent products that execute model-written code, and teams migrating off a rival sandbox SDK: drop-in shims exist for E2B, Daytona, Vercel and Blaxel.
isolation: Firecracker microVM on servers Runtime operates, with its own kernel; not a container and not gVisor. New sandboxes expose `/dev/kvm`, so nested virtualisation works. No GPU and no ARM: x86-64 only.
sizes: No fixed size menu: any vCPU / memory / disk combination inside the plan bounds. Pro allows 8 vCPU and 32 GiB; Growth 16 vCPU and 64 GiB; Scale 32 vCPU and 96 GiB. CPU is shared by default; reserved guarantees every vCPU at full price.

billing.model: A monthly plan whose fee comes back as usage: Pro $25 ($25 included), Growth $99 ($110 included), Scale $499 ($575 included). There is no free plan.
billing.meter: Per second: $0.03 per busy vCPU-hour measured, with a 100-millicore floor per sandbox, plus $0.008 per reserved GB-hour of memory. Running disk is $0.10 per decimal GB per 30-day month; paused storage is $0.18 per GB-month. Outbound traffic is $0.03 per GB with none free.
billing.stopped: A paused machine pays only for storage at the warm rate. Only delete ends the charge.
billing.planFee: Pro $25, Growth $99, Scale $499 a month. The fee returns as usage ($25, $110, $575). Yearly is 12 months for the price of 10.
billing.minimum: No minimum billing period. Signing up takes no card; creating a machine asks for one and starts a 7-day Pro trial with $5 of usage.

well: An agent that mostly waits: measured CPU with a 100-millicore floor makes an idle 2 vCPU / 4 GB hour about $0.04.
A small team that needs SSO, SCIM, a 400-day audit log and per-key spend limits without an enterprise plan.
Secrets that must not enter the machine, plus OIDC tokens for AWS or GCP.
badly: A buyer who needs a named founder, a funding history or a company older than a few months.
Multi-region or EU data residency: there is one region, in Virginia.
A workload that needs a Runtime-owned SOC 2 report.
A buyer who wants to stay on a free tier: there is no free plan. Signing up is free, but the first sandbox asks for a card and starts a 7-day Pro trial with $5 of usage.

usability.dashboard: Yes, a detailed console: a Home report with a Needs you section, sandboxes with Overview, Terminal, Files, Activity and Settings tabs, a limits page, and usage and billing with daily spend by product.
usability.withoutCode: Partly, and only for the first step: once a card is on file, one click on Home starts a sandbox with a shell in the page. There are no app templates; the documented no-code path is pasting its `llms.txt` link into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor.
usability.signup: Google or email sign-in and no waitlist. Signing up takes no card; creating a machine asks for one and starts a 7-day Pro trial with $5 of usage.
usability.docs: Extensive, every page dated, with `llms.txt` bundles. Support is an AI agent in the same call, with humans for billing, security and data loss. The status page is public and specific.
tripsUp: A sandbox is not a website host: nothing is reachable until you open a preview, domain or TCP port.
The bill moves while nothing happens, because memory is charged for every running second.
Pause, stop and delete are three different things with three different bills.
The first useful step still needs a command or an agent.
Memory is measured in GiB and disk in decimal GB, a 7.4% difference that shows up in quotes.
There is no EU region, and uptime was below the promised 99% during research.
There is no free plan: the first sandbox asks for a card and starts a 7-day Pro trial.

caveats.detail: Only delete ends the storage charge. A stopped box is a bill, not a cleanup, and `persistent: true` bills memory around the clock.

caveats.issue: Uptime was below the published promise
caveats.detail: On 12 November 2026 the API had passed 97.85% of checks over 30 days, below the 99% monthly promise, and 4 November passed only 61.38%; the last 7 days were 100%.

Signing up takes no card, but creating a machine asks for one and starts a 7-day Pro trial with $5 of usage. After that the cheapest plan is Pro at $25 a month, returned as usage. Cancelling pauses machines; their data is deleted 30 days later.

evidence.quote: Signing up takes no card. Creating a machine needs one

caveats.issue: The canonical state list is not published
caveats.detail: The docs name transitions and mention starting, running, pausing, paused, resuming, stopping and stopped, but there is no quotable list of state strings.
Everything runs in us-east. There is no EU option, and no per-tenant residency control.

A one-month-old repository, near-zero community discussion, and daily changelog entries including breaking changes. No preinstalled coding agents, and the vendor says no bridge harness has run on Runtime yet.

caveats.issue: The status page says no incidents while 4 November was 61.38%
caveats.detail: The incident list says no incidents are recorded, while the same page's daily table shows 4 November 2026 passing only 61.38% of API checks.

caveats.issue: Some products besides sandboxes are on the same meter
caveats.detail: Function calls ($0.20 per million) and CI/CD ($0.001 per vCPU-minute) now have published rates. This guide still prices only sandbox CPU, memory and disk.

strengths: Secrets the machine never holds: placeholders swapped into HTTPS headers for named hosts only.
OIDC workload identity that AWS and GCP can trust.
Pause with memory, and snapshots that keep memory by default.
Custom roles on Growth and above; SSO, SCIM and a year of audit log on Scale.
Billed on measured CPU, so a box waiting on a model costs the 100-millicore floor plus memory.
The Pro fee comes back as usage, and a 7-day trial includes $5.
